edges.description: Mediator-complex destabilization disrupts developmental and maintenance transcription, producing progressive widespread neurodegeneration.
The neurodegenerative process is accompanied by microcephaly.
The disease produces profound neurodevelopmental impairment.
Brain dysfunction produces an exaggerated startle response.
Cortical dysfunction produces refractory myoclonic seizures.

nodes.description: An exaggerated startle response with hyperkinetic movements is characteristic.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous MED11 C-terminal variant causes a lethal neurodegenerative disease.
evidence.snippet: The disease was characterized by microcephaly, profound neurodevelopmental impairment, exaggerated startle response, myoclonic seizures, progressive widespread neurodegeneration, and premature death.

nodes.description: MED11 is a subunit of the head module of the Mediator complex. The recurrent homozygous C-terminal p.Arg109Ter variant does not abolish the protein but disrupts its conserved C-terminus, impairing binding to partner subunits and destabilizing the MED11-MED22-MED17 four-helix bundle. This implicates Mediator-complex stability, rather than simple loss of protein, in brain development and neurodegeneration. MED11 belongs to the group of Mediator complex-associated disease genes.

evidence.snippet: Loss of the C-terminal of MED subunit 11 may affect its binding efficiency to other MED subunits, thus implicating the MED-complex stability in brain development and neurodegeneration.
